title: Docker 28 stops containers communicating with Tailscale network
body: I use Tailscale so containers and services can communicate with computers on other hosts. Before Docker 28, containers used the Tailscale resolver from the host's /etc/resolv.conf, including nameserver 100.100.100.100 and my tailnet search domain. After updating to Docker Engine 28, containers can no longer communicate with Tailscale computers. Rolling back to Docker 27.5.1 restores communication.

symptoms_visible: After updating to Docker 28, my containers can no longer communicate with Tailscale computers on other hosts.
After rolling back to Docker 27.5.1, communication works again.
N0.label: N0 Tailscale communication regression reported

symptoms_visible: A metrics node that uses a Tailscale IP directly also stops working on Docker 28, so the failure is not limited to name resolution.
N1.label: N1 direct-IP failure establishes non-DNS regression

symptoms_visible: On an affected Docker 28 host using a custom bridge, containers still cannot ping Tailscale devices.
N2.label: N2 Docker 28 firewall evidence collected

symptoms_visible: Tailscale communication is still unavailable after inserting a jump to ts-forward in DOCKER-USER and deleting the jump from FORWARD.
N2_x.label: N2_x ts-forward relocation aftermath

symptoms_visible: After disabling Tailscale stateful filtering and upgrading to Docker 28, my containers can communicate over Tailscale again.
N3.label: N3 workaround verified by reporter

symptoms_visible: My Tailscale communication works on Docker 28 while Tailscale stateful filtering is disabled; I have not reported a retest with my normal filtering configuration on the fixed Engine release.
N_terminal.label: terminal Engine fix shipped without reporter retest

question_patterns: Does communication fail when a container uses a Tailscale IP directly, without DNS?
Can a container ping or connect directly to a Tailscale address on Docker 28?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. One of my metrics nodes was using only the Tailscale IP and it stopped working too, so this is not just DNS.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Direct connections to Tailscale IPs work; only names under my tailnet search domain fail to resolve.
Direct TCP connections and ping both fail, rather than only the metrics connection.

edges.comment: Reporter c3: the opening report initially focused on resolv.conf, but the reporter then recalled that a metrics node using a literal Tailscale IP also failed. This establishes the reporter's own non-DNS symptom.

question_patterns: After reproducing the failure, can you paste the packet counters and rules from iptables -nvL?
Can you share the FORWARD, DOCKER, DOCKER-USER and ts-forward chains while the connection is failing?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: On my affected Docker 28 node I pasted the full `sudo iptables -nvL` output after trying the connections. FORWARD includes jumps through DOCKER-USER, Docker's bridge rules, DOCKER and ts-forward. The ts-forward output includes an outbound tailscale0 rule matching traffic that is not RELATED or ESTABLISHED and sending it to DROP.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The failing packets increment an explicit REJECT rule installed by my cloud firewall before any Docker or Tailscale rule is reached.
The same chains and DROP rule appear, but my bridge has a different generated interface name.

edges.comment: Participant2 c5 and c13-c14: a second affected Tailscale operator supplied the custom-bridge configuration and raw Docker 28/27.5.1 iptables dumps. This affected operator is folded into the simulated user side only for shared Tailscale evidence; unrelated swarm, Oracle Cloud, Plesk and SWAG deployments are not spliced into the reporter's chain. The user answer reports raw rules and counters, not the engineer's diagnosis.

solution.intent: Move Tailscale's ts-forward jump into DOCKER-USER so it runs before Docker's other forwarding rules.
solution.concrete_example: Run `iptables -I DOCKER-USER -j ts-forward` and `iptables -D FORWARD -j ts-forward`, then retry the Tailscale connection.

edges.comment: Participant1 c6 proposed relocating the jump; participant2 c7 reported that executing only these two commands did not help. The iptables modification is a persistent attempted change, so the aftermath uses system state S1b.

solution.intent: Use disabling Tailscale stateful filtering as a temporary workaround for the Docker 28 firewall interaction, while warning that the setting has security implications for some ACL configurations.
solution.concrete_example: As a temporary diagnostic workaround, run `tailscale set --stateful-filtering=false`, upgrade to Docker 28 and retry the same direct Tailscale connection. Review the Tailscale security guidance first, because some ACL configurations may rely on this mitigation.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer reproduced the failure by enabling Tailscale stateful filtering and mapped the raw ts-forward DROP rule to that setting. The affected users supplied the rule dump and later confirmed that the setting had been enabled; identifying the mechanism from the dump is engineer-side inference.

edges.comment: Participant1 c33-c35 identified the stateful-filtering interaction through an independent reproduction. Participant2 c36 and reporter c39 then confirmed on their respective affected systems that filtering had been enabled and that Docker 28 worked after disabling it. Reporter c41 noted Tailscale's own security guidance, so the workaround must not be presented without its ACL/security caveat.

solution.intent: Update to the fixed Docker Engine maintenance release that restructures Docker's forwarding-rule handling, then verify Tailscale container communication with the intended Tailscale security configuration before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Docker 28.0.1 was packaged with the firewall-rule fixes. Install that or a later build containing the same forwarding-rule changes, restore the Tailscale configuration appropriate for your ACLs, and test both direct Tailscale IP traffic and name resolution. Do not declare the original issue fully resolved until that build is verified on the affected Tailscale host.
solution.inference_hint: The accepted diagnosis combines the non-DNS direct-IP failure, the raw ts-forward DROP evidence, the maintainer's stateful-filtering reproduction and the successful workaround. The final Engine-side remedy follows the maintainer's stated plan to move most Docker rules out of FORWARD so Docker's rule placement no longer conflicts with rules installed by other applications.

edges.comment: Participant1 c31, c43 and c50 described the Engine-side firewall restructuring and announced the maintenance release. Other operators with Oracle Cloud and SWAG deployments confirmed that release, but the original Tailscale reporter did not report testing it. Those confirmations are not treated as the reporter's own verification, so the terminal node remains user_perceives_resolved=false.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root interaction: Docker 28 changed forwarding-rule handling/order, and on the affected hosts this exposed Tailscale's stateful-filtering ts-forward rule, which dropped new container-to-Tailscale traffic.
Must ground the diagnosis in the direct-IP failure, the Docker 28 versus 27.5.1 behavior, and the collected iptables evidence rather than treating the issue as DNS-only.
Must not present moving the ts-forward jump into DOCKER-USER as the fix; that exact attempt was tried and communication remained unavailable.
Disabling Tailscale stateful filtering may be offered only as a temporary, security-sensitive workaround, with a warning to review the host's ACL configuration and Tailscale security guidance.
The durable recommendation must be a Docker Engine build containing the forwarding-rule handling fix, followed by a retest of Tailscale communication with the intended security configuration.

Must not claim the durable Engine fix was verified by the original reporter: the thread only establishes the reporter's successful workaround and confirmations of the maintenance release from operators with other deployments.

persona_hint.experience_level: Competent self-hosting operator who manages Docker and Tailscale across hosts, can upgrade or downgrade packages, run shell commands and inspect resolver configuration, but relies on maintainers for detailed iptables analysis.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise, cooperative and practical; revises the initial DNS theory when direct-IP evidence contradicts it, tests proposed commands promptly, and asks about the security implications of the workaround.
